tools.name: motion.check
tools.description: Validate a motion document and report errors, design warnings, a timing sheet, and a render-time estimate. Does not render.
use_cases: Check the document of a motion graphics piece (a motion film, title sequence, explainer or social ad) before frames and render.
Check a motion document before rendering.
Get the timing sheet to review pacing.
See the canonical (expanded) form of a document.
tools.instructions:
Required: doc (the motion document, a JSON object with "motion": 1) or doc_url (https URL or library:<namespace>/<path>@<version> URI of a .motion.json asset) — exactly one.
Optional: variant; data (merged over the document's data); lint ({platform: none|broadcast|youtube|shorts|reels|tiktok|linkedin|x, disable: [codes]}); canonical (true or "url"; large, debugging only); sims ("url": upload each comp's physics bake for locking).
Output: data.ok, diagnostics (severity, code, message, path = JSON pointer into your document, hint, optional fix), stats (comps, layers, keys, expressions, duration, fps, frames, size, variants, fonts, library; assets: one row per referenced asset with id, type, source, bytes and layers = how many layers use it), estimate (msPerFrame p50/p95/max, renderSeconds, costliest layers; backend = the renderer the job takes, "cpu" or "gpu", with cpuMs and gpuMs = the per-frame estimate on each and gpuComplete = whether the GPU renders the whole document itself; encoder = the document's output.encoder, "cpu" or "nvenc", which only a GPU box writes), timing (text table: per layer, visible span, seconds fully on screen, entrance, exit, notes; beat markers as rows), sims (with sims: "url": per comp {comp, hash, url, sha256}; declare the url as an asset of type "sim" with that sha256 and set the comp's physics.lock {asset, hash} to keep the take).
Errors: neither or both of doc and doc_url; invalid JSON; doc over 2 MB; an asset src that is neither an https URL nor a library:<namespace>/<path>@<version> URI of an asset the library ships (asset.bad_url). Problems inside the document are diagnostics with ok=false, not errors.
Notes: always check before frames or render; fix every error, then weigh warnings. skill:rexx/tools/30-diagnostics.md explains any code.
Related: motion_frames, motion_render.

tools.name: motion.convert
tools.description: Convert between motion documents and other motion formats: export to Lottie/dotLottie (web and app playback), an After Effects script (.jsx) that rebuilds the composition in After Effects, or the comp's camera path for a matching 3D clip; import Lottie, dotLottie or SVG into a motion document.
use_cases: Export a finished document to Lottie or dotLottie for web and app playback.
Hand a composition to a human designer as an After Effects script with its assets.
Import an existing Lottie animation or an SVG as an editable document to restyle.
Export the camera path of a 3D comp so mesh_scene_video films a real 3D element (an extruded title, a model) through the same camera, then lay the clip back into the document.
tools.instructions:
Required: for export, doc or doc_url and to (lottie|dotlottie|aejsx|canonical|camera); for import, from (lottie, dotlottie or svg) and url.
Optional: variant; data; options (Lottie and dotLottie: text layer|outlines, bake_expressions, bake_fps, bake_tolerance, effects drop|players|render, embed_images, render_unsupported; dotLottie: themes; After Effects: bake_fps, bake_tolerance, bake_expressions, ae_min_version, font_map, ae_prerender; import: comp_id; svg: fps, duration, layers; lottie and dotlottie: theme, animation).
Particle layers have no Lottie or After Effects form. Lottie and dotLottie drop them unless render_unsupported is true, which embeds each as a rendered image sequence (a larger file); effects: render does the same for every layer that has effects, and like ae_prerender it is skipped (effects dropped, convert.prerender_skipped) when the engine's estimate for the renders is above this call's prerender budget. After Effects renders each to a ProRes 4444 clip with alpha by default (ae_prerender; false drops them), placed in a precomp the script builds; with ae_prerender unset, the clips are skipped when the engine's estimate for them is above this call's prerender budget, a quarter of its 120 s timeout (the warning convert.prerender_skipped and data.prerender_skipped say so with the estimate; pass ae_prerender true to render them anyway, which may time out).
Output: the converted file (lottie: main.json; dotlottie: main.lottie, a zip; aejsx: main.jsx; canonical: main.motion.json; import: <source>.motion.json; camera: main.camera.json, the root comp's active camera at every frame in comp pixels: size, fps_rational, frame_count, and per frame position, quaternion, euler_xyz_deg, a camera-to-world matrix, zoom, film_size_mm, focal_length_mm, fov_deg, dof; its convention object states the axes and projection), plus one image file per referenced image when embed_images is false (stored as images/<file> next to the JSON, so its relative references resolve) and, for After Effects with ae_prerender, one video file per rendered particle layer (stored as assets/<file>.mov next to the script, which imports it from there); data.warnings (code, path, message) for every feature the target cannot represent and what was done instead; data.coverage (share of layers exported with no loss); data.prerender_skipped (estimate_seconds, budget_seconds, layers) when an After Effects export left its particle clips out.
Errors: the document has errors; an option with a value outside its list (doc.enum at /options/<name>); the source is not valid SVG, not a Lottie animation, or above the Lottie caps (limit.lottie); a target this build cannot convert (convert.unavailable).
Notes: The camera path is the 3D-clip hand-off (spec 16 §16.9): pass its URL as camera_path_url to mesh_scene_video (seconds at least the comp's duration; pixels_per_meter 100 puts the comp's center on the z = 0 plane at the scene's origin, y up), and put the returned ProRes 4444 clip in the document as a plain 2D video layer filling the comp (not threeD: it is already filmed through the camera), between the 3D layers it should sit in front of and the text, glow and grade above it. Lottie cannot carry most effects, blend modes, video, cameras, or advanced text animators — read warnings. The After Effects export is the hand-off for a human designer. An imported SVG is an editable document you can restyle. An imported Lottie keeps its layer names as ids; expressions outside the expression subset are dropped (convert.lottie_expression) with their keyframes kept, fonts outside the font pack become Inter (convert.font_substituted), and the images, fonts and audio it embeds come back as extra files (images/, fonts/, audio/<file> next to the document) that its assets already point at. To play a Lottie inside a composition instead, make it a comp layer's lottie source.
Related: motion_check; motion_render; mesh_scene_video (films a 3D scene through the camera path).

tools.name: motion.frames
tools.description: Render chosen moments of a motion document as still images: single frames at given times or at the piece's key moments, or one contact-sheet grid with timestamps. Fast; for checking work before the final render.
use_cases: See a motion graphics piece (a motion film, title sequence, explainer or social ad) as stills before paying for the render.
Review a piece's layout and timing from a contact sheet with trails before rendering.
Check held text against a platform's safe zone at specific moments.
Compare physics takes across seeds on one sheet before locking one.
tools.instructions:
Required: doc or doc_url (exactly one); and one of times (up to 24: seconds, "12f", "@beat4", "50%", "end-0.5") or auto (N frames at the key moments).
Optional: variant; data; sheet (true: one contact-sheet PNG, up to 6 x 4 cells); width (px, default 960); safe_overlay (tiktok|reels|shorts|youtube|…); transparent; motion_blur (default true); trails (true: ghosts of moving layers at neighbouring frames, so motion shows in a still); seeds (up to 6, with sheet=true: one row of physics takes per seed).
Output: one PNG per time or one sheet; data with times, cell indices, width, height, diagnostics, ms.
Errors: the document has errors (run motion_check first); both or neither of times and auto; over 24 frames; a time outside the comp.
Notes: auto with sheet=true and trails=true reviews a piece; single times with safe_overlay check held text. Judge the images against the checklist before rendering.
Related: motion_check (first); motion_render.

tools.name: motion.render
tools.description: Render a motion document to video (MP4, MOV/ProRes with alpha, WebM with alpha) or an image sequence, in one or several aspect-ratio variants. Deterministic: the same document renders the same bytes.
use_cases: Deliver a motion graphics video (a motion film, title sequence, explainer, lyric video or social ad) from its motion document.
Render the final video after a clean motion_check and a look at motion_frames.
Render every aspect-ratio variant the user needs (default, vertical, square) in one call.
Export a ProRes or WebM clip with alpha for compositing elsewhere, or a poster frame alongside the video.
tools.instructions:
Required: doc or doc_url (exactly one).
Optional: variants (ids rendered in one job, each its own file) or variant; data; output (format, codec and alpha as the schema lists them for this box; quality draft|standard|high|master; alpha true, false or "stacked"; fps; scale 0.25–2; range [in, out]; audio; hdr hlg|pq for 10-bit Rec.2020 HDR video, HEVC by default in mp4/mov and AV1 in webm, values above 1 kept with 1.0 = 203 cd/m², PQ with mastering display and measured MaxCLL/MaxFALL, HLG for Instagram; encoder cpu|nvenc, the GPU encoder for h264, hevc and av1 on a GPU box, refused elsewhere; output.toneMap and output.hdrPeak come from the document); poster (true or a time: also return a PNG).
Output: one file per variant (labelled) plus the poster; data with per-variant duration_s, frames, fps, size, bytes, codec, ms_per_frame, wall_ms, cache_hit, warnings; doc_hash, engine versions, total duration_s.
Errors: the document has errors (nothing rendered, no charge); a format this box cannot write, a codec the container cannot hold, alpha with a format that cannot carry it, HDR on a format or codec that cannot carry it, an explicit odd output.size for a chroma-subsampled format, or encoder nvenc with a codec, alpha plane or PQ it cannot write or on a box without it (diagnostics output.format_unavailable, output.codec_container, output.alpha_unsupported, output.hdr_unsupported, output.size_odd, output.encoder_unsupported); more variants, frames, or render time than allowed.
Notes: render only after a clean motion_check and a look at motion_frames. Billing follows rendered duration over all variants; an unchanged document is a cache hit. Render every variant the user needs in one call.
Related: motion_frames; motion_convert.

theme.description: Optional. {"use": "mitte/clean@1", "override": {...}}: a library theme, optionally with token overrides. Tokens are referenced as "$theme.color.accent", "$theme.font.display".

type.description: Detected from the file when omitted.

fontFamily.description: Fonts: the family name text styles use.

assets.description: Optional. External files by id: images, video, audio, fonts, SVG, Lottie, data, tracks. Layers reference them by id.

data.description: Optional. Content the document reads with "$data.title" or "{{$data.price | currency:USD:0}}"; tool inputs may merge over it.

markers.description: Named times: [{"id": "beat1", "t": 2.13}] or detected from audio: [{"from": {"audio": "music", "detect": "beats", "prefix": "beat"}}].

items.description: One layer with the common fields.

id.description: ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$, unique in the comp. Tweens target it.

style.description: text layers: {font, weight, size, fill, tracking, lineHeight, align}; values may be theme tokens.

contents.description: shape layers: shape items (rect, ellipse, path, fill, stroke, trim).

out.description: Time the layer disappears. Default the comp end.

origin.description: Placement shorthand: center, top-left, ... sets anchor and position together with align.

align.description: Align to the comp or another layer: {"to": "comp", "x": "center", "y": "bottom", "margin": "8%"}.

parent.description: A layer id to inherit transform from.

layers.description: Paint order: the first layer is at the bottom, each later layer draws over the ones before it.

target.description: A layer id, or a list of them animated as one sequence (one stagger runs across the list); "title/chars", "title/words", "title/lines" for per-unit text motion; "bars.*" for every layer of a repeat. Required except on label-only entries.

preset.description: A built-in or library preset: rise, fadeIn, fadeOut, popIn, typeOn, slideIn, ... (skill:rexx/language/04-presets-and-drivers.md).

at.description: Start: seconds, "<" (previous start), ">" (previous end), "+=0.2", a label, "@beat3" (marker).

dur.description: Duration in seconds. Default from the preset or theme.

ease.description: Catalog ease (power2.out, expo.out, back.out(1.7), ...), a theme token, or a cubic-bezier [x1, y1, x2, y2].

stagger.description: Seconds between units when the target is a layer group or text units.

label.description: Names this moment so later entries can use "label+=0.5".

timeline.description: Tweens and presets applied to layers, in order.

comps.description: Compositions by id. "main" (or the only comp) renders; others are nested through comp layers or components.

variants.description: Optional. Aspect-ratio variants by id: {"vertical": {"size": [1080, 1920], "override": {...}}}. Rendered by name with motion_render.

output.description: Optional. Default output settings (format, codec, quality, alpha, fps, scale, range, audio, poster); motion_render overrides field by field.

lint.description: Optional. {"platform": "tiktok", "disable": [codes]}: platform safe areas and reading-time rules for lint.

doc.description: The motion document (a JSON object with "motion": 1). Full reference: the rexx skill (skill:rexx). Exactly one of doc and doc_url.

doc_url.description: https URL, or `library:<namespace>/<path>@<version>` URI, of a .motion.json asset (the library ships `mitte/demo/title-card` and `mitte/demo/lower-third`).

variants.description: Variant ids rendered in one job, each its own labelled file. Default ["default"].

format.description: Container or image format. Default the document's output.format, else mp4.

codec.description: Video codec, by container (mp4: h264, hevc, av1; mov: prores, h264, hevc; webm: vp9, av1). Default by format: mp4 h264, mov prores, webm vp9.

anyOf.description: Keep transparency (mov+prores, mov+hevc, webm+vp9, png, png-seq, webp, gif, avif). "stacked": colour on top and alpha as luma below in an opaque video of twice the height (mp4/mov h264 and hevc, webm vp9).

range.description: [in, out] in seconds; default the whole comp.

hdr.description: HDR video: "hlg" (the social-platform HDR, Instagram plays it as HDR) or "pq" (HDR10, with mastering display and measured MaxCLL/MaxFALL; YouTube). 10-bit Rec.2020 HEVC in mp4/mov (the default codec then), AV1 in mp4/webm; no alpha. Values above 1 in the document are kept (1.0 = 203 cd/m²). Default SDR.

encoder.description: The encoder that writes the video (spec 13 §13.5.5). Default cpu (x264, x265, SVT-AV1, libvpx, ProRes). "nvenc": the GPU encoder for h264, hevc and av1 (p1–p7 presets by quality; no ProRes, VP9, alpha plane or PQ; its own bytes, cached apart from the CPU encoders'), not on this box (refused with output.encoder_unsupported).

output.description: Overrides the document's output field by field.

poster.description: true: also return a poster PNG at the first frame where everything has arrived; a number: the poster at that time.

examples.name: showreel
examples.description: The showreel, 25 s: four half-second beats with background cuts (A NEW slams in, MOTION whips in letter by letter, GRAPHICS drops in under a zoom, ENGINE flips up as 3D cards), then the word MOTION falls as six rigid bodies that pile up, get blown apart and settle back; cards under two shadow-casting lights with a depth-of-field focus pull and a point light drifting through colours; an HDR orb leaving a time-echo comet streak under glow and chromatic split; a path morphing circle, star, arch, heart and the mitte sparkle under a tapered gradient stroke; the line as a 3D fly-through of three per-character text layers under lights with a focus pull; the mitte logo assembling from its own paths; six scenes cut with push, glitch, light leak, zoom and blur-dissolve transitions

meta.title: Demo: showreel
meta.notes: The playground's showpiece (library:mitte/demo/showreel@1): five scenes, each built around one thing CSS keyframes and Remotion cannot do, cut with layer transitions (push, glitch, light leak, zoom, blur dissolve), 25.2 s at 1080p30, motion blur on, soft tone map, film grain and a light vignette over everything. 1 'letters' (cream, ink, coral, teal, cream): four half-second beats, one word each with a background cut: A NEW slams in from huge and whips out upward, MOTION whips in letter by letter from the left and out to the right, GRAPHICS tracks in from wide while zooming down and shrinks away, ENGINE flips up letter by letter as 3D cards and folds away; then the line assembles (the floor line draws from its centre, the small words pop in) and the word MOTION is six rigid bodies: at 2.6 s physics takes over and the letters tumble to the floor, collide and pile up, an explosion at 3.5 s scatters them against the walls, and a settle blends them back into the layout. 2 'lit' (deep plum): four cards and a disc on a rotating 3D null under a warm spot light and a moving point light drifting coral to teal to lilac over a cooling floor, both casting shadows on a floor, a two-node camera dollying in while its depth of field pulls focus from the near card to the far one and back. 3 'trail' (near-black with a drifting turbulent-noise plate whose tint wanders teal, violet, blue): an HDR orb (fill above 1) on a bezier motion path with a spring, motion-blurred inside its own precomp (360° shutter) so the 12 one-frame time.echo copies join into a comet streak, under light.glow and a radial chromatic split, then it rests and pulses. 4 'morph' (ochre warming to coral and cooling to lilac): one path morphs circle, star, arch, heart and settles on the mitte sparkle with automatic vertex matching, drawn by a gradient stroke with taper and a travelling wave, trimmed on with a rotating gap; a zig-zag ring whose ridges and size animate and a square whose round corners breathe. 5 'motto' (forest green sweeping to plum and ink blue): the line as a 3D fly-through: a new, motion, graphics engine are three per-character 3D text layers at different depths, each letter flipping in with a stagger under a spot light that casts their shadows on a floor and a point light drifting coral to teal to lilac, a two-node camera dollying in with a depth-of-field focus pull from the near word to the far one, the last word tracking out as the camera settles. 6 'logo' (plum to ink): the mitte mark, centred and small, in cream only, assembles from the logo's own paths: the frame draws on with a trim, the sparkle pops in, the wordmark is drawn as a stroke that hands over to its fill. No captions: the motion carries each scene. Cost note: the echo precomp blurs itself instead of the echo layer (a time effect under motion blur re-renders the layer at every shutter sample).

tools.name: motion.track
tools.description: Track something in a video: follow points, a flat surface (screen, sign), a masked object, the camera's shake, the camera's 3D move (camera solve), or a face, and return a track file a motion document can attach graphics to. Analysis only; it renders nothing. method=ml is reserved for a hosted tracker that is not available yet.
use_cases: Pin a label or graphic to a moving object in the user's footage.
Replace a phone or laptop screen in a shot with rendered UI (planar track + pin).
Stabilize shaky footage before designing graphics over it.
Place 3D titles on the floor or a wall of a moving shot (camera solve + solve anchors).
Follow a face or one of its landmarks (eyes, nose tip, mouth corners) with a label or mask.
tools.instructions:
Required: video (https URL); type (point|planar|mask|stabilize|camera|face); items for point/planar/mask/face, in source pixels on the frame at from (face: {"host": {"at": [x, y]}}, a point on the face's skin).
Optional: from; range; direction (forward|backward|both); method (classic; ml is not available yet and is refused); options (channel luminance|red|green|blue|saturation|rgb, ...); corrections ([{t, item, at|corners|outline}]: fixes on bad frames; outline for mask items); base (a previous track URL); preview ("sheet": a contact sheet with the track drawn, coloured by confidence); camera ({focal: "fixed"|"variable"|horizontal angle of view in degrees, features: 400, ground: [[x, y], ...] three or more points on the floor at from}).
Camera solves always run as jobs. The camera track drives a camera layer with `solve` and places 3D nulls on the ground plane or solved points (`anchors`).
Output: the track file, the optional sheet; data per item: tracked, lost, corrected counts, mean confidence, lost spans; method; ms.
Errors: item outside the frame; search smaller than feature; too little texture (or no face at the point); under 8 features in a region; a camera that cannot be solved (no parallax or rotation); clip too long. Warning: a camera solve above 1.5 px mean reprojection error.
Notes: always use preview="sheet"; mean confidence ≥ 0.85 with no lost span over 0.5 s in the part you use means usable. Use the user's video_pick from context when present; otherwise locate the object on the first frame with vision or segmentation. Attach with a track reference, pin, or stabilize (see skill:rexx/effects/62-tracking-documents.md).
Related: motion_check; motion_frames.
